ISS-0001.title: runtime_char field bStatus_sleep_flag (offset 0x26) is a misnomer -- it is paralysis (麻痹), not sleep
ISS-0001.description: The runtime_char struct field at offset 0x26 is named bStatus_sleep_flag in Ghidra, but FD2 has no sleep ailment. Per fd2-knowledge (memory_hack.htm layout, which has a +8 header offset vs the Ghidra struct: KB 0x2E == Ghidra 0x26), offset 0x2E is 麻痹狀態 = paralysis status (set by 麻痹術 / Paralyze spell). A future Stage-2 struct cleanup should rename this field to e.g. bStatus_paralysis_flag and update all readers. Out of scope for this single-symbol refine (struct field, not the assigned function); recorded for follow-up. This refine corrected the src comment + plate annotation to say 'paralysis' without renaming the field.
ISS-0001.evidence: fd2-knowledge: query.py struct -> '0x2E XA: 麻痹狀態' (KB layout); KB-to-Ghidra +8 offset confirmed via team/job/HP fields; query.py grep '睡眠'/'沉睡' -> 'No match'; query.py grep '麻痹' -> 麻痹術 spell '2-4回合使敵人麻痹', 祛麻術 '解麻痹'. Ghidra get_struct_layout runtime_char: offset 38 (0x26) bStatus_sleep_flag, offset 33 (0x21) pStatus_flags_block[5].
ISS-0001.resolution: RESOLVED (closeout). Verified via fd2-knowledge (no 睡眠/沉睡 ailment; memory_hack 0x2E=麻痹狀態; +8 KB->Ghidra offset confirmed by poison 0x2D->0x25, paralysis 0x2E->0x26, silence 0x2F->0x27) and in-code semantics (battle.c counter-attack gate, chinit.c ch10 sets char 0x32/0x33=100, chend1.c clears, rndscene.c shake/palette). Renamed src field status_sleep_flag -> status_paralysis_flag across types.h + 8 .c (incl. awake/asleep/sleep-counter prose) and Ghidra runtime_char field bStatus_sleep_flag -> bStatus_paralysis_flag (offset 0x26); home plate 0x13fd4 de-misnomered. btl_aitg.c uses raw pChar[0x26] (already paralysis-commented), no change. Build PASS[RELOC] (field rename not emitted -> zero new binary delta).

ISS-0004.title: Ghidra plate calls the handler table at 0x51B91 '256 slots' but src globals.h declares it as [90]
ISS-0004.description: The chapter-event / post-action handler function-pointer table at 0x51B91 is indexed here by entry[4], a byte (potential range 0..255). The Ghidra plate for this function describes that table as a 256-slot 32-bit pointer array, whereas src/include/globals.h declares 'void (*data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_table[90])(uint32)'. This is a cross-cutting table-extent question (shared by fd2_handle_tile_event_interaction and fd2_process_battle_drop_entries), not a defect in this function's control flow, and the src comment makes no size claim, so nothing is changed at this stage. Flagged so the table's true allocated extent can be confirmed (data layout at 0x51B91) when the shared table is refined; if 90 is correct, this function's plate '256' wording is over-stated.
ISS-0004.evidence: globals.h:515 'extern void (*data_fd2_battle_ai_post_action_consequence_table[90])(uint32); /* 0x51B91 */'. get_xrefs_to(0x51B91) returns 3 code indexers: fd2_handle_tile_event_interaction@0x19511, fd2_fire_chapter_turn_events_for_phase@0x1a85a, fd2_process_battle_drop_entries@0x1ac1a. Ghidra plate text: 'fix_off32_00051b91 = 章節事件 handler table (256 槽位 32-bit function pointer 陣列 @ 0x51B91)'.
ISS-0004.resolution: RESOLVED (closeout). True extent = 90 entries, verified three ways: (1) next symbol data_fd2_battle_teleport_dest_world_x @ 0x51CF9 = 0x51B91 + 90*4 = 0x51B91+0x168, with no symbol in between; (2) btltab.c def comment '360 bytes = 90 x 32-bit function pointers, indexed by an 8-bit event id'; (3) Ghidra data PLATE+PRE at 0x51B91 both already say '90 x void(*)(uint32)' / '360B pointer[90], idx 0x00..0x59'. So 256 was wrong (256*4=0x400 would overlap teleport_dest+). Fixed: only the fd2_fire_chapter_turn_events_for_phase @ 0x1a813 function plate said '256 槽位' -> corrected to '90 槽位' + clarified event_id is a byte but only 90 slots allocated. The other two indexer plates were already fine (0x190ac no size claim; 0x1aa1d already '90 entries'). 8-bit-index-into-90-slot-table is the same vendor faithful-to-binary pattern as ISS-0014/0016.

ISS-0008.title: Pose-table global names read inverted vs their actual axis use
ISS-0008.description: The two per-chapter portrait pose-byte tables used to position the portrait icon have Ghidra/C symbol names whose X/Y axis semantics are swapped relative to their actual use. data_fd2_chapter_intro_portrait_pose_y_row_table @0x52635 is added DIRECTLY to the destination (within-row / X contribution), while data_fd2_chapter_intro_portrait_pose_x_column_table @0x52647 is MULTIPLIED by the 0x1C8 row pitch (row / Y contribution). The names therefore suggest the opposite axes. These are shared globals (also referenced by fd2_chapter_transition_with_intro, fd2_run_chapter_intro_menu_main/typeB/typeC), so this is NOT in scope for renaming under this single-function refine task; recorded for a future global-rename pass.

Ghidra primary symbols: 0x52635 => data_fd2_chapter_intro_portrait_pose_y_row_table, 0x52647 => data_fd2_chapter_intro_portrait_pose_x_column_table.
ISS-0008.resolution: RESOLVED (closeout). The paired swap was already applied in Stage 2 (handoff n=168/169): current Ghidra + src names are axis-correct -- 0x52635 = ..._pose_x_column_table (ADD direct @ 0x2D031 = X/within-row), 0x52647 = ..._pose_y_row_table (IMUL 0x1C8 @ 0x2D046 = Y/row). ISS-0012.title: Out-of-bounds frame read when terrain class exceeds the 5-entry table
ISS-0012.description: The handler indexes the 5-byte local item_id_table by tile_attr = tile_read_buf[2], the low byte of the +2 ushort terrain_class field, whose range is 0..0x1F. Only classes 0..4 select a defined table entry; classes 5..0x1F read past item_id_table[5] into adjacent stack-frame bytes. In the binary this is the literal frame read *(byte*)((int)&var_14 + var_1a); the emitted C item_id_table[tile_attr] reads whatever Watcom lays out after the 5-byte array, which is frame-layout dependent and not guaranteed bit-identical for out-of-range indices. Already tracked in tools/code_emit/data/emit_issues.json '000354fe' (type frame_layout_oob_index, severity low) and referenced by the source comment. Recording here for refine traceability; NOT fixing in this stage (it is a cut/unreferenced path -- no chapter FDFIELD hook reaches this slot with live tile data, so classes 0..4 are byte-identical and the OOB case is unreachable in real play).
ISS-0012.evidence: disasm 0x355AF MOV BL,[ESP+0x2]; 0x355B6 MOVZX EAX,byte ptr [ESP+EAX*0x1+0x8] (frame-relative index past the 5-byte item_id_table). Table = {0x1D,0x2B,0x33,0x3D,0x47} @ 0x5274E (5 entries). Only xref to 0x354FE is the DATA handler-table slot 0x51C79 (no tile-step/turn-event hook). emit_issues.json:756-766.
ISS-0012.resolution: RESOLVED (closeout; faithful-to-binary, no fix). Re-verified get_xrefs_to(0x354fe) = exactly ONE ref: DATA from 0x51c79 (the handler-table slot idx 0x3a). No CALL, no tile-step/turn-event hook reaches it; handler name __unref_pickup marks idx 0x3a as never dispatched by any chapter. The frame-relative OOB read for terrain classes 5..0x1F is faithfully reproduced and already tracked in emit_issues.json['000354fe'] (frame_layout_oob_index, low). Classes 0..4 byte-identical; OOB path unreachable in real play. By-design; conclusion recorded here + emit_issues.json.

ISS-0013.title: Unconditional close(handle) on LX magic mismatch ignores mode bit0
ISS-0013.description: On LX magic mismatch the function calls close(handle) without testing mode_byte&1. When called in in-memory mode (bit0==1), arg0 is a base address rather than a real file descriptor, so close() is invoked on a non-handle value. This is faithfully reproduced from the original binary (disassembly 0x363ea: PUSH EBP; CALL close at 0x3d01c is unconditional) and MUST NOT be changed -- the CRT-equivalent logic is verified to match FD2.LE. Recorded for awareness only. Practically unreachable: the sole (itself-dead) caller crt_equivalent_lx_module_loader_3647b only loads a valid LE image. The success-path close() at the end is correctly gated by bit0; only the mismatch error path is not.
ISS-0013.evidence: disassemble_function 0x00036344: at 0x363e8 JZ skips to 0x363f5 (match path); fall-through 0x363ea PUSH EBP / 0x363eb CALL 0x0003d01c (close) then JMP 0x3638a (return 0), with no TEST of [ESP+0xe0]&1 guarding it -- contrast the success-path close at 0x36451 TEST byte ptr [ESP+0xe0],0x1 / JNZ 0x36464.
ISS-0013.resolution: RESOLVED (closeout; faithful-to-binary CRT-equivalent, MUST NOT change). Disasm re-verified: mismatch path 0x363e8 JZ 0x363f5 else fall-through 0x363ea PUSH EBP / 0x363eb CALL 0x3d01c (close) is UNCONDITIONAL (no mode-bit0 test) then JMP return 0; success-path close at 0x36451 IS gated (TEST [ESP+0xe0],0x1 / JNZ 0x36464). Entry 0x3635b tests bit0 -> in-memory mode (bit0=1) makes EBP a base address not a handle. Exactly matches FD2.LE; intentionally preserved (Layer-2 equivalence). Reachability: sole caller crt_equivalent_lx_module_loader @ 0x3647b has 0 callers (dead) and only loads valid LE images, so the mismatch path never triggers. No fix.

ISS-0014.title: Dispatch table indexed by full byte (0-255) but emitted as a 10-entry array
ISS-0014.description: chunk_type is a uint8 (0-255) used to index data_fd2_animation_ani_decoder_frame_dispatch_table, which the Layer-2 port declares as [10] (src/table/anitab.c, src/include/globals.h). The original binary's table at 0x5276A is also exactly 10 pointers (verified: the 10th pointer ends at 0x52792, followed by 4 zero bytes then the 'Stack Overflow!' literal -- not an 11th entry). So both binary and port assume well-formed ANI.DAT streams emit only opcodes 0-9; a malformed byte >= 10 would read past the array in both. This is faithful to the original (not a port-introduced regression) and ANI.DAT is a trusted bundled asset, so it is informational only -- no change in this stage.
ISS-0014.evidence: Decoder: src/anim/anidec.c L74-77 indexes table[chunk_type] with chunk_type from *g_ani_cursor++. Table decl: src/include/globals.h L527 'extern void (*...frame_dispatch_table[10])(void);' and src/table/anitab.c L480. Binary extent: read_memory(0x52792,48) = 00 00 00 00 'Stack Overflow!\r\n' confirming exactly 10 entries; first entries 0x36AE7,0x36B01,... match handler addresses.
ISS-0014.resolution: RESOLVED (closeout; faithful-to-binary, info-only, no fix). read_memory(0x5276a,48) re-verified: exactly 10 LE dword pointers (0x36AE7/0x36B01/0x36B0F/0x36B51/0x36B8A/0x36BB2/0x36BCE/0x36C13/0x36C2C/0x36C56) spanning 0x5276a..0x52791, then 4 zero bytes at 0x52792 + 'Stack Overflow!' literal -> no 11th entry. src declares [10] (globals.h:527, anitab.c:481). Decoder indexes table[chunk_type] by a full byte; both binary and port assume ANI.DAT emits only opcodes 0-9 (trusted bundled asset), so a >=10 byte over-reads in both -> faithful, not a port regression. No fix.

ISS-0015.title: Run-length prose was off by one and used a byte-overflowing expression (now corrected)
ISS-0015.description: Both the src comment and the Ghidra plate previously described the 0xC1..0xFF run marker as producing '(b - 0xC1) + 2 pixels total' / 'Run length = (byte + 0x3F) + 1 = 257..319 pixels'. The binary computes run_remain via SUB AH,0xC1 on an 8-bit register, giving (b - 0xC1) in 0..0x3E = the number of ADDITIONAL pixels beyond the one painted at marker time. Total pixels painted of that value = (b - 0xC1) + 1 = 1..63. This was a comment/documentation inaccuracy only; the C statement '((b - 0xC1) << 8) | next' is correct and was not changed. Both the src comment and the Ghidra plate have been corrected during this refine.
ISS-0015.evidence: Disassembly @ 0x4E925-0x4E92B: MOV AH,AL; SUB AH,0xC1; LODSB ESI; RET (AH is 8-bit, result 0..0x3E for b=0xC1..0xFF). State-machine trace: marker call writes 1 pixel and sets run_remain=(b-0xC1); each subsequent call with run_remain!=0 writes 1 pixel and decrements, giving (b-0xC1) further writes; total = (b-0xC1)+1. For b=0xC1 -> run_remain=0 -> exactly 1 pixel.

ISS-0016.title: Table extent (30) is shorter than the full spell-id index space (max 0x23=35)
ISS-0016.description: Spell IDs reach 0x23 (35), but the table is 30 bytes (indices 0..29) and the reader copies exactly 30 bytes into a 32-byte stack scratch. For spell_id >= 30 (sword skill 音速刃 0x1E=30 and summons 0x20-0x23) the indexed byte load reads beyond the 30 copied bytes (into the upper, uninitialised slots of the 32-byte local). This is the vendor binary's own behaviour, faithfully reproduced: the C array holds the exact 30 vendor bytes and the reader copies exactly 30 as the original does, so it is NOT a rebuild equivalence bug. It is the same buffer-larger-than-table pattern used by the sibling tables in this file (e.g. the 25-byte projectile table in a 28-byte buffer). High-ID offensive effects most likely route through other visual paths; left as-is per Layer-2 functional-equivalence goal. No fix in this stage.

ISS-0017.title: pose X/Y table pair (0x52635, 0x52647) names are swapped vs blit math
ISS-0017.description: 0x52635 is named '..._pose_y_row_table' but is added directly to the destination (within-row/X); 0x52647 is named '..._pose_x_column_table' but is multiplied by the 0x1C8 row pitch (row/Y). The two names should be swapped together in Stage 2 so each name matches the axis it actually supplies. Recorded as a paired rename: 0x52635 -> '..._pose_x_within_row_table', 0x52647 -> '..._pose_y_row_table'. No logic change.
ISS-0017.evidence: fd2_render_chapter_intro_overlay disassembly: 0x2D031 'MOVZX EDX, byte ptr [EAX + 0x52635]' then 0x2D044 'ADD EDX,EBX' (EBX = base+0x8088) = direct add; 0x2D046 'MOVZX EAX, byte ptr [EAX + 0x52647]' then 0x2D04D 'IMUL EAX,EAX,0x1C8' = multiply by row pitch. ISS-0017.resolution: RESOLVED (closeout) with ISS-0008. Names were already swapped-correct in Stage 2: 0x52635=...pose_x_column_table (X, added @ 0x2D031), 0x52647=...pose_y_row_table (Y, *0x1C8 @ 0x2D046) -- verified vs disasm + all 5 readers (rndmenu.c, chtrans.c, chintro.c usage all consistent: x_column->src_cx, y_row->src_cy of fd2_blit_scaled_chapter_pose). No rename needed (x_column/y_row are already axis-correct; the proposed x_within_row was only an alternate wording). Cleanup only: rewrote 0x52635/0x52647 Ghidra PLATEs to clean axis-correct text, cleared stale 0x52647 PRE, fixed chtrans.c:477. Comment/plate-only -> zero binary change.

Note the sibling const option-templates in the same file (e.g. data_fd2_ui_inline_action_menu_template) ARE already const, so the state-template family is inconsistent with them.

ISS-0021.title: Co-dead orphan chain is emitted as const data + accessor, but pipeline_spec rule E-7e says it may be skipped
ISS-0021.description: rebuild_info/emission/pipeline_spec.md rule E-7e classifies (data_fd2_orphan_table_60181 + fd2_get_orphan_table_60181_entry) as a co-dead data+accessor chain (accessor has 0 callers / 0 LE-FIXUP targets; Watcom keeps both only via mutual reference) and prescribes skip_unreachable_data + skip_unreachable_code (emit neither). The current src DOES emit both (orphan.c defines the table, table.c defines the accessor). This is functionally safe -- emitting extra unreachable const bytes plus a never-called accessor does not change behaviour -- but it is a discrepancy between the documented emit policy and the actual src. Not a correctness/equivalence bug; flagged for the post-workflow emission-policy reconciliation (decide whether to honor E-7e and drop the chain, or update E-7e to record that this chain is intentionally emitted). Out of scope for this comment/name refine.

ISS-0022.title: Live movement_cost_table buried inside a stale 'orphan/dead' byte[856] data unit in Ghidra
ISS-0022.description: In Ghidra the symbol data_fd2_battle_movement_cost_table @0x61646 is only a label inside a single defined Data unit byte[856] spanning 0x615FD..0x61954 whose primary symbol is data_orphan_615fd_856b_leading_prefix_final_unreachable_unknown. The PRE_COMMENT on that unit (at 0x615FD) classifies the whole 0x615FD..0x61954 range as a dead/orphan/unknown leading prefix of a once-1024-byte weapon-animation blob. That classification is wrong for the 0x61646 sub-region (and for the adjacent 0x6188A job_allowed_items_table): both are LIVE, read by real accessors. The 856-byte unit actually covers orphan-prefix (0x615FD..0x61645, 73B) + movement_cost_table (0x61646..0x61889, 580B) + job_allowed_items_table (0x6188A..0x61954, 203B) = 856B exactly. Because the symbol has no code unit of its own at 0x61646, it has no own PLATE/PRE; the only nearby descriptive comment lives on a different symbol (0x615FD), so it is out of scope for this single-symbol refine and not editable here without restructuring the array (a multi-symbol layout change). The C source already represents these correctly as separate typed const arrays, so emit/codegen is unaffected; only the Ghidra annotation is misleading.

Symbols: 0x61646 primary=data_fd2_battle_movement_cost_table; 0x6188A primary=data_fd2_battle_job_allowed_items_table.
